title: Weight-Space Programming with Claude Mythos: Weight Edits and Implanted Circuits in a 0.8B Language Model, with Transfer to an Engineering Surrogate
read_level: full (English pages 1-4 of the 8-page bilingual PDF; German pages 5-8 not read). Zenodo record/API returned HTTP 403 ('unusual traffic'); PDF read from the author's Hugging Face repos (keyvan-ai/Mythos-WSP-Loopbreaker-Skill, identical file in keyvan-ai/Mythos-WSP-Qwen3.5-0.8B), whose header states 'Version 1.0, 7 November 2026 · DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24036187'. Zenodo description obtained via DataCite API. Identity with the Zenodo-hosted file not verified byte-for-byte.
metadata_mismatch: Metadata title includes the suffix '(bilingual: English / German)', not in the PDF title. Corpus abstract was empty; DataCite abstract matches the PDF abstract.
why_wsp: Claude Mythos 5.1 as editing agent rewrites Qwen3.5-0.8B weights (rank-3 projection; then repurposes four MLP units into a written repetition-detector/termination circuit) and edits a 4,804-weight thermal surrogate MLP from physical-parameter identification, without gradients.
facets: application domain: LLM math reasoning; power-electronics thermal surrogate
domain: LLM math reasoning (reasoning loops, MATH-500); engineering surrogate (MOSFET junction temperatures)
editor: Claude Mythos 5.1 (Anthropic); control run with locally operated Qwen3.8-27B on surrogate task
interface: code/tensor tools (agent in run folder with forward-pass tool; activation access via teacher-forced passes)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (fixed forward-pass budget: 10 passes for Exp. 1, 8 further passes for Exp. 2)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Exp 1: "a rank-3 projection in three attention matrices (0.785 % of parameters)"; Exp 2: "four units of MLP layer 23" repurposed; Exp 3: "four tensors, 13.4 % of the weights"

headline_results.quote: MATH-500 rises from 7.3 % (our own measurement of the original) to 32.5 % through a rank-3 projection in three attention matrices
after 8 further passes the model reaches 58.7 % (SE 1.1) and the share of truncated answers falls from 66 % to 17 %
58.7 % on MATH500 (SE 1.1 over samples, 1.9 over problems; math-verify 55.4 %)
the unmodified model reaches 42.8 % with thinking disabled
In the MIT study, GPT-6 Astra reached 12.3 % at the same budget, 14.1 % with 25 passes and 48.1 % with 50 passes.
0.17 K mean error at full load, versus 2.3 to 4.5 K for gradient fine-tuning on the same data and 0.07 K for retraining on 5,000 simulations
A control run with a locally operated Qwen3.8-27B reached 0.03 K, but in violation of the rules

cost.claim: Forward-pass budgets only; no token, time or $ figures found
cost.quote: after 10 forward passes ... after 8 further passes
Generation ran on vLLM 0.33 (one RTX PRO 6000 or one RTX 4000 Ada)

baselines_and_controls: Original model re-measured (7.3%); thinking-disabled original (42.8%); MIT GPT-6 Astra figures at 10/25/50 passes (quoted, not rerun); reported reproductions (51.0%); surrogate: unchanged surrogate, affine recalibration, gradient fine-tuning (output layer / all weights / CV config), retraining on 5,000 sims (upper bound).
runs_and_variance: MATH-500 with 4 samples per problem (2,000 answers); SE over samples and over problems reported. Single editing run per experiment. Quote: 'Standard errors are given over samples and over problems.' (Sec 2)
robustness_of_edits: not tested ('GSM8K, MGSM and a capability battery for side effects are pending'); surrogate tested on extrapolation to full-load range
verification: Hidden test sets; deterministic solver as verifier for surrogate; complete call logging. No formal verification.
limitations_stated: One LM and one benchmark protocol; side-effect battery pending; surrogate physics small and known in equation form; 'Edits do not add knowledge that is present neither in the network nor in the available data.'
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming, MIT CSAIL 2 Nov 2026, and logs github.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs
notes_for_survey: Single-author report replicating the MIT Qwen3.5-0.8B loop repair with a different editor at a 10-pass budget, then implanting a 4-neuron circuit; adds a thinking-disabled control (42.8%) absent from the MIT study. Non-peer-reviewed; single run per experiment.
